strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds Rust-owned remote HTTPS candidate acquisition before activation or replacement.
Fetched candidates are parsed and compiled through the existing Mode Pack permission validator before cache commit.
Successful candidate fetches persist bounded summaries and idempotent cache evidence without raw candidate JSON in ledger/RPC payloads.
Headless callers can acquire a remote Mode Pack candidate deterministically and decide whether to review or replace active policy.

answers.strategic_capabilities: mode_pack_runtime with support from runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: modepack.fetchCandidate performs an explicitly authorized HTTPS fetch, validates URL/network/content boundaries, compiles the Mode Pack, and caches a replay-safe candidate snapshot by content fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing local activation/replacement/rollback only consume workspace-local .brownie/modepack.json or prior lifecycle evidence; they cannot acquire remote candidates.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Pack acquisition remains manual and cannot participate in headless autonomous policy update workflows.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M37.1 replacement and M37.2 rollback because it does not mutate active policy; it creates a validated remote candidate cache boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. Existing RPCs either read modes or mutate active snapshots and cannot perform authorized network fetch/cache.
answers.no_new_summary: No new report wrapper is added; the RPC returns the bounded execution result required for the fetch/cache action.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime can make a bounded HTTPS request, reject unsafe destinations/content, compile external Mode Pack JSON, write a controlled cache, and return replay-safe evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled caller can acquire and fingerprint candidates before deciding on replacement without manual file edits.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the first M38 acquisition primitive; later phases can review trust and feed approved candidates into active replacement.

exit_criteria: Only HTTPS URLs without credentials, fragments, unsupported ports, localhost, or private/link-local resolved addresses are accepted

Redirects, non-200 status, oversized responses, invalid UTF-8, unsupported content type, sensitive-like content, invalid JSON, unsafe permissions, and duplicate built-in mode IDs are rejected before cache commit
expected_content_sha256 is validated when supplied and mismatch fails closed
Successful fetches persist normalized candidate cache under .brownie/modepack-candidates by content fingerprint
Replaying the same successful content returns the existing cache event id and does not append duplicate ledger evidence
RPC and ledger payloads return bounded summaries only and contain no raw Mode Pack JSON or raw ledger payload
Behavior tests cover cache/replay, URL denial, and content fingerprint mismatch

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M38.1 changes runtime/protocol/store acquisition behavior and dependencies; review must confirm it is bounded remote candidate fetch/cache, not activation or wrapper surface.
